pages.text: "Ouch!" Nils the little bear slid through mud outside the cabin. His blue boots skidded, and his knee scraped a stone. Spring rain had made the ground slippery.
His knee stung, and tears filled his eyes. Yet he shut his mouth tight. "I'm a big brother, so I don't cry. It doesn't hurt at all. I'll play more!" Nils sprang up.
Even crouching to roll a pinecone wasn't fun. His shoulders kept rising and jerking. His nose wrinkled, and his throat felt blocked.
Grandpa Bruno bent his knees, eye to eye. "Let's see." The scrape stung. He said softly, "Holding it in makes your shoulders shake."
Nils shook his head. "Big brothers don't cry." Grandpa opened both paws wide. "You can cry here. Come."
At those words, his tightly shut mouth opened by itself. "Waaah!" Nils buried his face in Grandpa's green vest and cried all he needed. Grandpa patted his back. "Tears coming? Let them out!"
After a long cry, his blocked throat felt open. Nils sniffled and peeped up. "Now... I'm okay." One round tear mark spread on the vest.
Grandpa washed the knee with tub water and wrapped it in clean cloth. "After crying, hurt feels a little lighter." Nils nodded, and his shoulders relaxed.
Now Nils knew what to do when tears came. "One, say it hurts! Two, don't hold tears in! Three, hug Grandpa!" He lifted both paws high.
Grandpa sat Nils on his lap and patted his back. Crying doesn't stop you being a big brother. Only a vest mark remained; the hurt had gone. Nils grinned. "Tears coming? Let them out!"
